Equilibrium momentum shift

A particle that oscillates in a stationary RF bucket ($\varphi_s=\pi$, below transition) does not have mean relative momentum zero. The RF phase returns to itself after a synchrotron period only if the mean time of flight matches the RF period. With a nonlinear slip factor that condition fixes a nonzero mean

\[\delta_{\mathrm{eq}} =-\frac{\eta_1\langle\delta^2\rangle+\Lambda}{\eta_0},\qquad \Lambda=-\frac{2\pi}{C}\bigl(J_x\xi_x+J_y\xi_y\bigr).\]

Here $\eta_0,\eta_1$ are the time-of-flight slip coefficients, $\xi_{x,y}$ the linear chromaticities, and $J_{x,y}$ the Courant–Snyder actions. For a linear synchrotron oscillation $\langle\delta^2\rangle=\delta_m^2/2$. A cubic truncation of the RF waveform multiplies the $\eta_1$ piece by $1-\hat\varphi^2/32$ and shifts the synchrotron frequency by $\Omega/\omega_s=1-\hat\varphi^2/16$. That correction is second order in the actions and is not kept in the normal form below.

The RF is a thin energy kick at one point of the ring. A finite-length cavity has its own closed-orbit offset in $\delta$; that is a separate study.

From the torus

The one-turn map is the Lie product of the magnetic factors and the thin kick. After the linear symplectic normalisation and the homological removal of non-resonant generators, motion is uniform rotation of three phases at three fixed actions. The torus of those actions is the set of all triples of phases. Laboratory $\delta$ is a function on that torus. $\delta_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the average of $\delta$ over the whole torus:

\[\delta_{\mathrm{eq}}=\delta^\ast+d_x J_x+d_y J_y+d_s J_s.\]

For thin RF at $\varphi_s=\pi$, $\delta^\ast=0$. The coefficients $d_k$ are the quadratic part of the sixth component of the normalising transformation, averaged over angles. They do not use $\eta$ or $\xi$. Substituting $\delta_m^2=2\sigma_\delta^2 J_s$ into the formula above reproduces them to relative $10^{-6}$:

$d_x$ [1/m]$d_y$ [1/m]$d_s$ [1/m]
torus average0.146652440.22328941$2.477064\times 10^{-3}$
formula0.146652570.22328971$2.477064\times 10^{-3}$

Element-by-element symplectic tracking of the unexpanded Hamiltonians, with the exact thin kick, gives the same $\delta_{\mathrm{eq}}$ to a few parts in $10^3$ at $\delta_m\le 10^{-3}$. The residual grows as $\delta_m^2$ (the next order, not kept). A long time average equals the torus average when the tunes are incommensurate. The torus itself is not built from the tracking samples.

The mean energy also receives a kinematic piece from $\langle\delta^2\rangle$:

\[\Delta E_{\mathrm{eq}} =\beta_s^2 E_s\Bigl(\delta_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac{\delta_m^2}{4\gamma_s^2}\Bigr).\]
